clue.text: Racket made by Conservative group drinking coffee

indicators.note: whatever drinks takes something inside itself, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
a milky espresso drink
a ring is a circle or clique of people

explanation.surface: A party faction makes a din over its morning coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: The Conservative and the group join as C plus RING, and the coffee goes between them, so CLATTERING.
explanation.definitionFit: A clattering is a loud rattling noise, which is one kind of din or racket.

clue.text: 27 possibly dunked in overturned ice bucket

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an ice cube in a bucket, but 27 is BREAKWATER, and reading icE BUCket backwards gives CUBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakwaters are commonly armoured with large concrete blocks of a standard shape called cubes, so one is an example.

clue.text: Horse advanced on watering hole, moving north

a pub or bar, where people go to drink

explanation.walkthrough: 'Watering hole' looks like a pond for the horse, but it is slang for a pub; only that piece goes backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arab is a well-known breed of horse, famous for endurance and a dished face.

clue.text: First attempt to film lead in Sleeping with the Enemy? Don’t rush

indicators.note: the lead of anything is what goes in front, so only the opening letter is wanted

the word's opening letter
time is called the enemy, as in the saying that time is the enemy of us all

explanation.surface: A director shooting the opening take of the film Sleeping with the Enemy is told to go slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: Sleeping with the Enemy is a real film title, which hides the split: S from Sleeping, then TIME as the old enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: To take one's time is to proceed slowly without hurry, so the phrase is an instruction meaning go slowly.

clue.text: Say what pupil unhappy on results day may demand

definitions.text: what pupil unhappy on results day may demand

blocks.note: first meaning: to comment or observe

blocks.clueFragment: what pupil unhappy on results day may demand
blocks.note: second meaning: a fresh grading of an exam paper, read as RE- plus MARK

explanation.surface: A student disappointed with exam grades asks for them to be checked again.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word as re-mark, the British term for having an exam script marked again after an appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark is to state or comment on something, and a re-mark is an exam paper graded a second time.

clue.text: Race coming from a particular country

blocks.note: first meaning: a famous British steeplechase run at Aintree, known by this one-word short name
second meaning: belonging to or typical of one nation

explanation.surface: An ethnic group traced to a single homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' reads as ethnicity, but it means a horse race: the Grand National, run at Aintree, is often called simply the National.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand National steeplechase is commonly shortened this way, and the adjective describes things belonging to one nation or state.

clue.text: Output of powerful server right for computer company

blocks.note: in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch

explanation.walkthrough: 'Server' suggests computing next to the computer company, but it is a tennis player serving.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is a Taiwanese manufacturer of laptops and desktop machines, a well-known brand of computer maker.

clue.text: Sweet lover I see with incredibly chic, cool clothing

clue.text: French article called to stop widespread firing here

the French masculine definite article

clue.text: Wants Cambridge University to probe case of British forger

explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge University points to the English one, but it is the American Cambridge and its MIT. A forger here is one who forges metal, not documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith works iron at a forge, hammering hot metal into shape, so he literally forges things.

clue.text: Nincompoop‘s rot loudly dismissed once

explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' looks like it means formerly, but it says only one of the two Fs goes from GO OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A goof is informal for a silly or foolish person, a synonym for an idiot or clown.

clue.text: Crafty behaviour by two card players who unfortunately eclipse others

taken as written, to be rearranged

clue.text: Group that supports flogging swine after odd capers

explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like it places the swine, but it is part of the letters that caper. Flogging is British slang for selling.

clue.text: Leaders in Scottish Parliament lampoon Speaker – Speaker who’s struggling

one who utters is one who speaks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' twice suggests the parliamentary chair, but the first is just one who speaks and the second starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A splutterer talks in a confused, choking rush of words, so is someone finding speech difficult.

clue.text: Is inspiring note on fieldwork inspiring?

N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' appears twice: first it means breathing in and so holding a letter, and at the end it is the definition. Fieldwork here is literal farm labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Instilling an idea or feeling gradually puts it into someone's mind, much as inspiring does.

clue.text: Mull wine I won’t initially place on the counter

a flat refusal
the word's opening letter

clue.text: Notorious player of Chelsea’s beginning like a star

a, plus a nova, a star that suddenly flares in brightness

clue.text: Car salesman is above being critical of others

a number is something that numbs, and ether is an anaesthetic

taken as written

clue.text: Somewhere in Norway beside tree, shivering? One might call you cold
